SNAKE BITE
Introduction
A neglected tropical disease. In Africa, snake bite often occurs among farmers who walk unshod, and occasionally occur around homes when snakes are accidentally stepped upon.

Causes
Poisonous snakes belong to the families of:
- Viperidae (responsible for most snake bites in Africa)
  - Subfamilies: Viperinae (old world vipers), Crotalinae (New world vipers, Asian pit vipers)
- Elapidae (e. g. cobras)
- Colubridae (e. g. boomslang)
  - A large group; only a few species are dangerously toxic to humans
- Hydrophidae (sea snakes)
